children.text: It has been said the new vaccine called RTS,S or Mosquirix, aims to trigger the immune system to defend against the first stages of malaria when the plasmodium falciparum parasite enters the human bloodstream through a mosquito bite.

Statistics from the World Health Organisation show that every 2 minutes, a child dies of malaria. The disease is mostly in sub-Saharan Africa and is said to be tackled by using insecticide-treated bed nets and drug treatments to reduce spread.

Some say the vaccine's effectiveness is low compared to jabs for other diseases. However, malaria claims so many lives that the WHO believes it will still prevent tens of thousands of deaths every year.

"This long-awaited malaria vaccine is a breakthrough for science, child health and malaria control. Using this vaccine in addition to existing tools to prevent malaria could save tens of thousands of young lives each year." - Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, @WHO.
